 SALT LAKE CITY (KUTV) — Bodum USA is recalling about 5.9 million French press coffee makers with replaceable glass carafes because the carafe can break during use if it is cracked or damaged. Stirring coffee with a metal spoon can damage the glass, creating a risk of serious burn injuries.
 The recall covers 8- and 12-cup Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper and Kenya models. They were sold at Target, Walmart and other retailers, as well as online, from 1974 through October 2026 for about $15 to $65.
 Consumers should stop using metal spoons or utensils to stir coffee in the carafe and contact Bodum for a free plastic stirring spoon and warning label. Bodum has received 70 reports of carafes breaking, including 48 reports of burn injuries.

 RootStim is recalling about 11,000 bottles of three 5% minoxidil hair-regrowth treatments containing rosemary, with or without biotin. The bottles are not child-resistant, creating a potentially deadly poisoning risk if children swallow the contents.
 The treatments were sold on Amazon from August 2025 through February 2026.
 Consumers should secure them away from children and contact RootStim for a replacement. Customers must mark the bottle “RECALLED,” discard it and email a photo to finergraceing@gmail.com. No incidents or injuries have been reported.
